just_in.title: How to Make Marble Clay Diyas for Diwali, Step by Step
just_in.excerpt: White clay, bright colours rolled to a marbled 1/4 inch, a pinched tip, 45 minutes in the oven and gold rims — a Diwali craft children can actually do.
just_in.image_caption: A clay diya, the traditional oil lamp decorated and lit for Diwali (file photo)
just_in.nri_angle: Diaspora families can make marble diyas this weekend with standard US craft-store clay and tea lights, a day ahead of Diwali gatherings.

steps.detail: Line a baking tray with parchment paper; roll white clay out as the base layer with a rolling pin.
Place cubes of coloured clay on the white, roll together and work by hand to a 1/4-inch thickness; stacking colours before rolling changes the swirl.
Cut a round with a cookie cutter or small bowl, shape it into a small bowl, and pinch one tip to a point.
Bake on the tray in a preheated oven at 265 degrees F for 45 minutes.
Cool to room temperature, paint the rims gold, and let the paint dry.
Set a tea light in each finished diya instead of oil and a wick for a mess-free lamp.

lifestyle-health.title: How to Make Marble Clay Diyas for Diwali, Step by Step
lifestyle-health.excerpt: White clay, bright colours rolled to a marbled 1/4 inch, a pinched tip, 45 minutes in the oven and gold rims — a Diwali craft children can actually do.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A clay diya, the traditional oil lamp decorated and lit for Diwali (file photo)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Diaspora families can make marble diyas this weekend with standard US craft-store clay and tea lights, a day ahead of Diwali gatherings.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.detail: Line a baking tray with parchment paper; roll white clay out as the base layer with a rolling pin.
Place cubes of coloured clay on the white, roll together and work by hand to a 1/4-inch thickness; stacking colours before rolling changes the swirl.
Cut a round with a cookie cutter or small bowl, shape it into a small bowl, and pinch one tip to a point.
Bake on the tray in a preheated oven at 265 degrees F for 45 minutes.
Cool to room temperature, paint the rims gold, and let the paint dry.
Set a tea light in each finished diya instead of oil and a wick for a mess-free lamp.
